independence: NICE, RCH, WHO, CDC and Queensland are distinct authoring bodies; shared neonatal studies are not independent replications. RCH cites NICE and ASID, with its own clinician-authored diagnostic and antimicrobial guidance. Both RCH pages count once; WHO chapter and summary count once; NICE guidance and surveillance count once. NCBI is only WHO host.

issues.resolution: RCH uses48h and NICE72h. Public entry does not turn either threshold into a universal diagnostic rule.
US universal pregnancy screening and UK risk-based prevention are explicitly separated.

NICE samples before second dose for third-dose decisions; QCG samples before third and withholds pending level in its protocol. Public text uses local monitoring, without delaying urgent initial infection treatment.
WHO hospital courses/referral-impossible alternatives are not universal home prescriptions. Local response, culture, infection focus and professional support govern the public explanation.
